text:
Maya (Design): Sharing early mocks for a compact 'rule composer' that handles thresholds, routing, and suppression. Two main tradeoffs I'm debating: compact single-row rules with expandable details vs stacked cards, and whether channel routing should show full badges inline or a condensed "routing" pill that opens a popover. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE

Omar (PM): Scanability is key for SREs. We need a dense list view by default, expand for details.

Liam (Eng): Agree on dense rows. Stacked cards add a lot of DOM and hurt scroll perf on pages with hundreds of rules. Also avoid rendering heavy avatars or icons per-row.

Sasha (Accessibility): Accessibility checklist: when expanding a row, maintain logical focus (don't jump to the end of the list). Expose the expanded region as a labeled region and add an aria-live="polite" update for the sample preview so screen reader users know it changed.

Priya (Product): Copy nit: 'suppress until' feels vague. Suggest 'suppress notifications until' or 'mute channels until' depending on scope. Also propose showing an estimated alert volume badge (low/med/high) to help prioritization.

Evan (Design): For the header, shorter placeholders + a tooltip for longer help text keeps rows compact. I prototyped a small 'volume' token next to the rule name.

Nina (Design): Instead of full channel badges per row, show a "routing" pill with a channel count (e.g., "3 channels"). Clicking it opens a small anchored panel with the channel list and toggles. Keeps rows tidy.

Liam (Eng): That sounds implementable. Use an anchored popover for the channel panel, set aria-expanded on the pill, and avoid nesting another modal. Will prototype keyboard focus wrap for the popover.

Sasha (Accessibility): Popover guidance: role="dialog" with aria-modal=false; trap focus while open, ensure Escape closes and returns focus to pill. Provide keyboard shortcut to jump to the routing pill from the rule list.

Maya (Design): Idea: add a 'sample voice' selector (Ops / On-call / Manager) in the sample preview to show how notifications read for different audiences. Thoughts?

Priya (Product): Like that, but hide it behind a small 'sample settings' chevron so it doesn't add visual clutter for new users. Also track that sample changes are reflected in the aria-live region.

Evan (Design): Contrast alert: tiny filled channel pills drop below AA on dark backgrounds. Use a bordered mini-pill style for small sizes. Example CSS to try: ```border: 1px solid #CED4DA; background: transparent; color: #17202A;```

Liam (Eng): Also prevent long channel names and emoji from blowing out row height. Use text-overflow: ellipsis and normalize emoji line-height.

Maya (Design): Plan: implement compact rows with click-to-expand, routing-pill -> popover, sample settings hidden under chevron, and bordered mini-pills. I'll update Figma and post next iteration. Thumbs if you agree.

Priya (Product): :thumbsup:

Sasha (Accessibility): +1 — please include the aria-live and focus management details in the spec doc.

Liam (Eng): +1 from infra, will prototype focus behavior and perf checks.
